key_insight: Critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes adapt gradient descent to local curvature, promoting convergence toward flatter interpolating minima.
engineering_relevance: CDP offers an adaptive stepsize approach with a SAM-like flattening effect, including in reported experiments on pre-trained LLM fine-tuning.
method: Multiply the classical Polyak stepsize by 4 and a mild damping factor.
Use critical equioscillations near the minimizer manifold while damping drives convergence.
At small loss, projected iterates approximately descend log maximum Hessian eigenvalue along the minimizer manifold.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports uniform-in-time sharpness and loss-reduction guarantees for locally quadratic Morse–Bott losses, plus flattening experiments on nonlinear teacher–student networks and LLM fine-tuning.
watch_item: The guarantees require local Morse–Bott structure; empirical flattening beyond this regime does not establish the same convergence guarantees.
paper_title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
